skill_traces.query:
Andrew: Hi Audrey! I had a great hike last weekend with some friends and my girlfriend at the spot we found recently. Nature was so peaceful – it was so nice to just relax and take it in. How's your week been? Anything exciting going on lately?
Audrey: Hey Andrew! That hike sounds great. Nature is good for the soul, right? My week's been good - taking care of my four doggies and making sure they're happy and healthy took up most of my free time. Also, exciting news! I signed up for a workshop about bonding with my pet next month. Can't wait to learn new stuff and strengthen my bond with my pets. What's up with you?
Andrew: That's awesome! Glad have the opportunity to bond with your pets. That workshop sounds cool. Where did you hear about it? And the one in the picture is adorable!
Audrey: I know right? I saw this workshop flyer at my local pet store. It was a positive reinforcement training class and I wanted to give it a shot. The volunteer in the store was nice enough to let me meet their dog – he was so friendly and playful!
Andrew: Cool! Positive reinforcement can really help you bond with your dogs. Do you think they'll catch on quickly?
Audrey: I'm sure they'll catch on really quick! They're quick learners and love rewards! Can't wait to learn how to train them better.
Andrew: That's awesome! Keep me updated on their progress.
Audrey: Definitely! I'll keep you updated on how it all goes and how my pups are doing. Fingers crossed they'll be extra behaved. And I'll let you know some tips on training your future dog as well!
Andrew: Thanks! I'm excited to hear about it. Have a great time at the workshop!
Audrey: I'll definitely have a good time and make the most of it. I'm sure this is a must learn for any dog owner.
Andrew: You think so? Wow, you must be a good salesperson because I'm almost sold on this class haha.
Audrey: Haha, I just think its important to have pets learn how to behave on a positive reinforcement way. Punishment is never the proper way for pets ya know?
Andrew: Yeah I would't want to be punished, let alone puppies and dogs.
Audrey: Right!? I don't want to hurt any of my dogs. Just by thinking of it gives me pain.
Andrew: Yeah I feel you. Anyways, let me look into their classes. I'll talk to you soon, have fun!
Audrey: Yup, ttyl!

selected.name: Extract Pet Activity Memories
selected.description: When a user mentions doing an activity with their pet (e.g., walking, hiking), during extraction.
content: During extraction, treat any explicit statement where the speaker describes performing an activity with their pet as a candidate memory, even if it appears in casual sign-off or small talk.
Record the activity and the pet name as the object (e.g., 'walks with Buddy', 'hikes with Toby'), with the speaker as the subject.
Resolve relative time from the message timestamp; if the activity is described as a general habit, capture it as a state; if it is a one-off event, capture it as an event.
Stop after capturing the stated activity; do not infer additional pet facts or unrelated activities unless explicitly mentioned.
selected.rerank_reason: The conversation includes explicit mentions of activities with pets, such as hiking and training, which directly trigger the extraction of pet activity memories.

nearby_not_selected.description: When a user reflectively describes a past shared activity with a specific person and frames it as bonding, making memories, or quality time.
content: During extraction, treat first-person statements about a past shared activity with a named person that explicitly mention bonding, making memories, closeness, or quality time as a durable event or relationship memory candidate.
Capture the activity, the companion, and the relational framing.
Do not require explicit fact-like phrasing; reflective storytelling is sufficient evidence.
Create at most one candidate per distinct activity-and-companion pair, and skip statements that name no specific person or activity.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.

nearby_not_selected.name: AggregateRepeatedVisitCounts
nearby_not_selected.description: When a message shows a person visiting a place and existing memories record an earlier visit by the same person to the same place, create or update a memory stating the total number of visits.
content: During extraction, when a message states that a person visited a place and another message in the session already establishes an earlier visit by the same person to the same place, generate a candidate memory containing the cumulative number of visits; do not expand this to other places or trips.

During CRUD, when adding or updating a visit event, search the retrieved memory pool for prior visits by the same person to the same place; if found, add a compact visit-count memory or update the existing one so the total count is explicit.
Only aggregate same-person, same-place visits; do not count different locations, do not add a count memory when no prior visit exists, and stop once the count is recorded.
